title: Analytic leakage suppression with a single control field: fast two-qubit gates with tunable couplers
authors: Lukas Heunisch, Michael J. Hartmann, Aashish A. Clerk
abstract: Simple analytic pulse-shaping techniques are of great practical utility in quantum control, with prime examples being the DRAG method for suppressing leakage in superconducting microwave gates and the transitionless-driving approach to shortcuts-to-adiabaticity. Standard versions of these methods require two orthogonal control channels, with the second channel effectively breaking time-reversal symmetry. This appears to rule out their use in settings with only a single real-valued control field, such as the kind of baseband flux control that is common in many superconducting circuit architectures. We show here that a simple analytic pulse-shaping technique derived via a Magnus expansion is effective even with just a single baseband control channel. We demonstrate its efficacy by simulating a two-qubit gate between transmons realized with a tunable coupler and baseband flux pulses. Our corrections dramatically reduce non-adiabatic leakage caused by ramping the coupler: for realistic device parameters, leakage in a fast iSWAP gate is suppressed by up to three orders of magnitude. Our approach is general, goes beyond simply suppressing unwanted spectral weight at leakage transitions, and can be applied to a variety of platforms.
summary: This paper introduces a novel analytic pulse-shaping technique to mitigate leakage errors during fast two-qubit gates in superconducting qubits. By utilizing a Magnus expansion, the authors derive a correction pulse that effectively cancels non-adiabatic leakage caused by the time-varying coupler. This method is highly valuable as it works even when only a single baseband control field is available, significantly boosting gate fidelity.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of suppressing non-adiabatic leakage errors during fast two-qubit quantum gates when the control mechanism is limited to a single real-valued control field.
main_result: A novel analytic pulse-shaping technique, derived via a Magnus expansion, was shown to suppress leakage in a fast iSWAP gate by up to three orders of magnitude for realistic superconducting circuit parameters.
method: The authors derive a correction pulse by applying a Magnus expansion to the Hamiltonian in the adiabatic frame, allowing them to cancel the non-adiabatic error terms generated by the time-varying coupling.
model_or_system: The system modeled is two superconducting transmon qubits coupled by a tunable coupler, whose dynamics are controlled by baseband flux pulses. The analysis focuses on the evolution between instantaneous eigenstates (dark and bright states).
key_observables: Non-adiabatic leakage population into the coupler state, and the resulting gate fidelity (e.g., $1-f$ for CZ gate).
important_parameters: Gate time ($t_g$), coupling strength ($g$), detuning ($\Delta(t)$), and the required correction pulse amplitude ($\delta\omega(t)$).
main_assumptions: The method is derived using a Magnus expansion truncated to first order, and the analysis assumes the system can be effectively described in the adiabatic frame.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic architecture, the time-dependent detuning profiles, and the population evolution comparing bare pulses versus the corrected pulses, showing leakage suppression.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem (leakage with single control fields), develops the Magnus-based analytic correction technique, and then validates this technique by simulating two-qubit gates (iSWAP and CZ) against established methods.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, general, and analytically derived tool for designing quantum control pulses in superconducting circuits, overcoming the limitations imposed by single-parameter control fields common in hardware.
